Part I — Endorsement Library

This part collects all 96 model endorsements from FAA AC 61-65K (issued 11/14/2025), grouped into 13 color-coded categories that mirror the browse view of the Simply Endorsed app. Each card shows the verbatim model text from the Advisory Circular, plain-English notes, who may sign the endorsement, and how long it remains valid; chips on each card link to related endorsements inside this book and to the referenced regulations on eCFR.

Student Pilot

14 endorsements

Pre-Solo

Student pilot prerequisites before first solo: TSA eligibility, student pilot certificate, and medical qualification.

Before most airplane students can exercise PIC solo privileges, they need a student pilot certificate, required medical qualification, and the pre-solo training endorsements. Dual instruction may begin before these are fully in place.

Prerequisites before solo

TTSA citizenship / eligibility verification

Flight training providers must handle TSA citizenship or eligibility verification when applicable. If the logbook-endorsement method is used, AC 61-65K A.14 provides commonly used language.

49 CFR § 1552.15(c) AC 61-65K, A.14

IStudent pilot certificate application

Apply through IACRA or an acceptable paper process with an authorized person such as a CFI, DPE, ACR, or FSDO representative. It is not an IACRA-only process.

14 CFR § 61.83 14 CFR § 61.85

MMedical certificate / qualifying medical status

For most private-path airplane students, solo requires at least a third-class medical or another qualifying medical basis that fits the operation being conducted.

14 CFR § 61.3(c) 14 CFR § 61.23

TSA Citizenship / Eligibility

TSA citizenship or eligibility verification is a training-provider compliance item and is separate from the FAA student pilot certificate and separate from medical qualification.

Key Points

  • Training providers must follow applicable TSA citizenship or eligibility verification procedures before providing covered flight training
  • If the provider uses the logbook-endorsement method for U.S. citizenship verification, AC 61-65K A.14 contains commonly used endorsement language
  • This step does not replace the student pilot certificate and does not replace the required medical qualification

Student Pilot Certificate

A student pilot certificate is required before solo flight, but it is not required to begin dual flight instruction.

Eligibility

  • Minimum age 16 for airplane (14 for glider or balloon)
  • Must be able to read, speak, write, and understand English

Application Process

  • Application may be made through IACRA (iacra.faa.gov) or by paper in a form acceptable to the Administrator — 14 CFR 61.85 does not limit the method to IACRA only
  • An authorized person (CFI, DPE, ACR, or FSDO representative) verifies identity and processes or forwards the application as required
  • The FAA does not charge a fee when the certificate is processed through a FSDO; a school, examiner, or other processing entity may charge its own fee

Certificate Issuance & Duration

  • The permanent certificate is mailed; a temporary student pilot certificate may become available in the applicant's IACRA console after processing
  • Student pilot certificates issued after April 1, 2016 no longer expire in the old 24/36-month way — they are generally surrendered when upgrading to a higher certificate
  • Solo endorsements are placed in the logbook, not printed on the student pilot certificate itself

Documents to Carry on Solo Flight

  • Student pilot certificate
  • Photo identification
  • Medical certificate or other qualifying documentation as applicable

Medical Certificate

A separate medical qualification is generally required before solo flight for the normal airplane/private training path. The student pilot certificate and medical qualification are separate requirements and should not be confused.

  • Third-class medical is the typical requirement for most student pilots training toward private or recreational airplane privileges
  • Medical class depends on the privileges being exercised — not simply the highest certificate a pilot may someday hold
  • Commercial privileges generally require at least a second-class medical when those privileges are exercised
  • ATP PIC privileges generally require a first-class medical when those privileges are exercised
  • Some students may qualify under exceptions or different pathways (sport pilot, glider/balloon, certain 61.113(i) operations)

How to Obtain a Medical

  1. Complete the MedXPress application online before your appointment
  2. Schedule an exam with an FAA-designated Aviation Medical Examiner (AME)
  3. Obtain the medical early — do not let it delay solo training

Solo Timeline

  1. Start dual instruction
  2. Apply for the student pilot certificate
  3. Complete TSA citizenship/eligibility verification if applicable
  4. Obtain the required medical qualification
  5. Complete pre-solo aeronautical knowledge test and flight training
  6. Receive the appropriate solo endorsements
  7. Exercise solo privileges only when all required elements are satisfied

Solo privileges may be exercised only when these prerequisites and applicable endorsements are satisfied.

Resources & Regulations

  • IACRA — Integrated Airmen Certification and Rating Application
  • FAA Medical Certification
  • MedXPress — FAA Medical Application
  • Find an Aviation Medical Examiner (AME)

Primary endorsements

A.3

Pre-solo aeronautical knowledge

Standard CFI signoff No expiration
14 CFR § 61.87(b)
AC 61-65K verbatim · AC page A-7

I certify that [First name, MI, Last name] has satisfactorily completed the pre-solo knowledge test of 14 CFR § 61.87(b) for the [make and model (M/M)] aircraft.

  • Proves the student understands the aircraft, rules, and local procedures before flying alone.
  • Helps confirm the student knows emergency actions and operating limits.
  • Prevents a first solo from happening before the student has the needed knowledge base.

Pre-solo flight training

Standard CFI signoff No expiration
14 CFR § 61.87(c)(1) and (2)

I certify that [First name, MI, Last name] has received and logged pre-solo flight training for the maneuvers and procedures that are appropriate to the [M/M] aircraft. I have determined they have demonstrated satisfactory proficiency and safety on the maneuvers and procedures required by 14 CFR § 61.87 in this or similar make and model of aircraft to be flown.

  • Shows the student can safely control the airplane without the instructor onboard.

  • Gives the instructor a documented basis for allowing solo flight.

A.6

Solo flight (first 90-calendar-day period)

Standard CFI signoff 90 calendar days
14 CFR § 61.87(n)
AC 61-65K verbatim · AC page A-8

I certify that [First name, MI, Last name] has received the required training to qualify for solo flying. I have determined they meet the applicable requirements of 14 CFR § 61.87(n) and are proficient to make solo flights in [M/M].

  • This is the student’s main legal authority for first solo flight.
  • Limits the solo to the specific make and model the student was trained in.
  • The 90-day limit forces regular instructor oversight.
solo student pilot

Also include if you are using the TSA citizenship logbook endorsement method.

A.14

Endorsement of U.S. citizenship recommended by the Transportation Security Administration (TSA)

Standard CFI signoff No expiration
Title 49 of the Code of Federal Regulations (49 CFR) § 1552.15(c)
AC 61-65K verbatim · AC page A-9

The flight instructor must keep a copy of the documents used to provide proof of citizenship for 5 years or make the following endorsement in the student’s logbook and the instructor’s logbook or other record used to record flight student endorsements with the following: I certify that [First name, MI, Last name] has presented me a [type of document presented, such as a U.S. birth certificate or U.S. passport, and the relevant control or sequential number on the document, if any] establishing that they are a U.S. citizen or national in accordance with 49 CFR § 1552.7(a).

  • Documents that citizenship verification was completed when using the endorsement method.
  • Helps the instructor show compliance with TSA flight training security requirements.
  • Protects both instructor and student if records are later reviewed.

Night Solo

Night solo training and authorization endorsement.

Primary endorsements

A.5

Pre-solo flight training at night

Standard CFI signoff 90 calendar days
14 CFR § 61.87(o)
AC 61-65K verbatim · AC page A-8

Flight training must be received within the 90-calendar-day period preceding the date of the flight. I certify that [First name, MI, Last name] has received flight training at night on night flying procedures that include takeoffs, approaches, landings, and go-arounds at night at the [airport name] airport where the solo flight will be conducted; navigation training at night in the vicinity of the [airport name] airport where the solo flight will be conducted. This endorsement expires 90 calendar days from the date the flight training at night was received.

  • Night flying is harder because of reduced visual cues and common illusions.
  • Helps ensure the student knows runway lighting, night procedures, and night judgment.
  • The 90-day limit keeps that night training recent.
solo student pilot

Repeated solo cross-country flights not more than 50 NM from the point of departure

Standard CFI signoff No expiration

I certify that [First name, MI, Last name] has received the required training in both directions between and at both [airport names]. Student solo in Class B airspace and at a Class B airport.

Primary endorsements

A.12

Solo flight in Class B airspace

Standard CFI signoff 90 calendar days
14 CFR § 61.95(a)
AC 61-65K verbatim · AC page A-9

I certify that [First name, MI, Last name] has received the required training of 14 CFR § 61.95(a). I have determined they are proficient to conduct solo flights in [name of Class B] airspace. [List any applicable conditions or limitations.]

  • Class B is high-workload airspace with heavy traffic and tighter ATC expectations.

  • The 90-day limit keeps that approval current.
